info.title: AWS Events API
info.description: API for AWS event data: browse events, browse their sessions, and manage your schedule.

get.description:
Lists AWS events. Returns ongoing and upcoming events by default; set includePast to also include
events that have already ended.

parameters.name: includePast
parameters.description: Include events that have already ended. Defaults to false (ongoing and upcoming events only).

schema.description: Include events that have already ended. Defaults to false (ongoing and upcoming events only).

get.description:
Gets a single AWS event by id, with the same fields as a list entry. Not filtered by date: an event that has
already ended is still returned, so a link to a specific event keeps working after the event is over.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event to retrieve.

schema.description: The event to retrieve.

post.description:
Marks one or more sessions as favorites for the caller. Requires attendee sign-in for the event. A favorite
records interest only; it does not reserve a seat. Individual sessions can fail while others succeed, so a 200
does not mean everything was added; always read `failed`. A session already favorited is reported there too, so
re-sending a request is not a safe retry.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event the sessions belong to.

schema.description: The event the sessions belong to.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

schema.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

delete.description:
Removes one session from the caller's favorites. Requires attendee sign-in for the event. Removing a session
that is not favorited is a 404, so this is not a safe blind retry.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event the session belongs to.

schema.description: The event the session belongs to.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session to remove from favorites.

schema.description: The session to remove from favorites.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

schema.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

post.description:
Adds a personal time entry to the caller's schedule: a block of time that is theirs, not a session. Requires
attendee sign-in for the event.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event to add the personal time entry to.

schema.description: The event to add the personal time entry to.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

schema.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

delete.description:
Removes a personal time entry from the caller's schedule. Requires attendee sign-in for the event. Removing one
that is already gone succeeds, so a retry is safe.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event the personal time entry belongs to.

schema.description: The event the personal time entry belongs to.

parameters.name: personalTimeId
parameters.description: The personal time entry to remove, as returned by GetSchedule.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

put.description:
Replaces a personal time entry. Requires attendee sign-in for the event. A full replacement: every field is
required, and any optional field left out is cleared.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event the personal time entry belongs to.

schema.description: The event the personal time entry belongs to.

parameters.name: personalTimeId
parameters.description: The personal time entry to replace, as returned by GetSchedule.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying, in seconds.

sessions can fail while others succeed, so a 200 does not mean everything was reserved; always read `failed`.
A session already reserved is reported there too, so re-sending a request is not a safe retry.

sessionIds.description: The sessions to add as favorites.

AuthenticationRequiredExceptionResponseC.description: This event is not available anonymously. The response's `WWW-Authenticate` header says where to authenticate.

BulkFailure.description: One session a bulk request was refused for.

sessionId.description: The session this failure refers to.

conflictsWith.description:
The caller's already-scheduled sessions that overlap this one, when the refusal was a time clash. Absent
for every other kind of refusal, and never empty when present.

BulkFailureCode.description:
Why one session in a bulk request was refused, as a stable value safe to branch on.

Treat an unrecognized value as a generic refusal: values are added as the event platform grows, and a client
that switches exhaustively on today's set would break on the next one.

BulkResult.description:
The outcome of a bulk request, which can succeed for some sessions and fail for others. A request is
reported per session: check `failed` even on a 200.

successful.description: The sessions the request was applied to. Empty when none succeeded.

failed.description: The sessions the request was refused for, each with a `code`. Empty when everything succeeded.

eventId.description: Unique event identifier, stable across requests.

eventType.description: Event series or category, e.g. "AWS Global Summit".

startDate.description: Start date and time, ISO-8601 with UTC offset.

endDate.description: End date and time, ISO-8601 with UTC offset.

isOnline.description: Whether the event takes place online rather than at a physical venue.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the event is scheduled in, e.g. "America/Sao_Paulo".

timezoneAbbreviation.description: Short timezone abbreviation for display, e.g. "BRT".

timeFormat.description: Preferred time-of-day display for the event, either "12 hour" or "24 hour".

supportedLanguageCodes.description: BCP-47 language tags this event supports.

authenticationRequired.description: Whether the event's deeper content requires attendee login.

EventAuthRequiredExceptionResponseConten.description: The caller is signed in but not registered for this event.

EventNotFoundExceptionResponseContent.description: The requested event does not exist (or is not publicly listed).

EventsServiceExceptionResponseContent.description: The service could not process the request due to an internal error.

EventsUnavailableExceptionResponseConten.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. Retriable: clients should back off and retry.

items.description: The events in this response. Empty when there are none.
This page of sessions, ordered by `sessionId`. Empty when the event has no published sessions.

totalCount.description: The number of sessions in the event's catalog.

nextToken.description: Pass as `nextToken` to fetch the following page. Absent on the last page.

OperationUnavailableExceptionResponseCon.description:
This operation has been intentionally disabled and is not accepting requests at this time. Retrying will not
help until it is re-enabled.

PersonalTime.description: A personal time entry on the caller's schedule.

personalTimeId.description: Identifies this entry, for update and removal.

startDateTime.description: When the block starts, written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` in UTC (e.g. "2025-12-02T16:00:00").

endDateTime.description: When the block ends, in the same form as `startDateTime`.

location.description: Free-text location of the block, when one was given.

PersonalTimeInput.description: The values of a personal time entry: a block of the caller's own time on their schedule, not a session.

startDateTime.description:
When the block starts, written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` (e.g. "2025-12-02T16:00:00"). Always UTC, so a trailing
"Z" or an offset such as "+01:00" is rejected rather than converted. A block is stored to the minute, so the
seconds must be `00`.

endDateTime.description:
When the block ends, in the same form as `startDateTime`. Must be after `startDateTime`, and the length
between the two must be a whole number of 5-minute increments.

location.description: Free-text location of the block. Optional.

PersonalTimeNotFoundExceptionResponseCon.description:
The personal time entry is not on the caller's schedule: either it never existed, it was already removed, or it
belongs to another attendee. All cases share this one error because a caller cannot act on them differently.

An unknown event on these routes is also a 404. The two are separate errors in the model but share the status, so
a generated client sees one 404 response; read the message to tell them apart.

Schedule.description:
One attendee's schedule for an event. Every list is present, and is empty rather than absent when it has no
entries. The session lists carry ids; look a session up to get its details.

reserved.description: Sessions the attendee holds a seat reservation for.

favorites.description: Sessions the attendee marked as favorites. A favorite is interest only, not a reservation.

SeatAvailability.description:
How full a session is, as a band rather than a count. Present only on reservable sessions. `walkUp` means
no reservation is taken; attend by walking up.

Session.description: A single session within an event.

sessionId.description: Unique session identifier, stable across requests.

level.description: Difficulty or audience level, e.g. "300 - Advanced".

isAllDaySession.description: Whether the session spans the whole day.

isReservable.description: Whether the session accepts seat reservations.

topics.description: Technology domains the session covers, e.g. "Artificial Intelligence".

industries.description: Industries the session is aimed at.

roles.description: Job roles the session is aimed at, e.g. "Data Scientist".

services.description: AWS services the session covers, e.g. "Amazon SageMaker AI".

customerPersonas.description: Customer personas the session is aimed at, e.g. "Architect".

experiences.description:
Named programs the session belongs to, e.g. "Executive Summit". Attendance may be restricted to that
program's participants.

additionalActivities.description: Additional activities associated with the session.

focusAreas.description: Focus areas the session is tagged with.

SessionNotFoundExceptionResponseContent.description:
The requested session is not available: either the session does not exist within the event, or the event
itself does not exist. Both cases share this one error because a caller cannot act on them differently.

SessionTime.description: When and for how long a session runs.

timezone.description: Timezone the date and time are given in, when the source provides one.

ThrottlingExceptionResponseContent.description: The caller has made too many requests in the current window and should retry later.

ValidationExceptionResponseContent.description:
The request could not be accepted as sent: a field is missing, too long, or malformed, or the request was
refused as a whole. The message says which. Not retriable: the same request will be refused again.
